absent: Report buffer allocation sizing and host submission details are not shown.
Generic zone callback validation and disk publish details are not shown.
Remainder of queue limits handling after the zoned model switch is not shown.
Request submission, status translation, unmapping and completion internals are not shown.
Workqueue lifecycle, freeze handling and teardown ordering are not shown.
Defaults for request queue, poll queue and queue depth tunables are not shown.
Numeric values of feature bits, zone states, opcodes and error mappings are not shown.

findings.text: Host configuration access is typed with endian conversion and requires sleepable context. Narrow members use a single transport fetch, wider members use a batched fetch, feature gated reads signal absence when the bit is not negotiated, single byte writes go through the transport setter, and queue discovery delegates to the transport finder with affinity hints.
The block personality publishes geometry query, disk teardown and zone reporting. Geometry and teardown are always available while zone reporting is available only when zoned support is compiled in.

The multiqueue personality publishes submission including batched submission, commit, completion, queue mapping and polling. Mapping spreads per type queue counts with affinity appropriate to interrupt and poll queues, and batch completion releases per request resources before ending the batch.

Device attributes publish a serial identifier and a cache mode control within a single null terminated group. The cache control stays readable when configurability is absent and otherwise uses default visibility.

Zone reporting requires configured zone_sectors and a live attachment, is bounded by remaining request count and buffer capacity per device round, stops when the device reports no further zones or capacity ends, returns the count of successfully reported zones when positive and otherwise signals invalid argument.

Device fields z_type and z_state map to generic type and condition with pointer handling. Empty and closed keep reported position, full moves the pointer to zone end, the two open variants map to explicit and implicit open, not write pointer maps to its condition, and readonly and offline force the pointer to maximum. Unknown type or condition is reported as a device error with input output failure.

Host managed zoned limits require non zero write granularity which also sets physical size and minimum size, non zero power of two zone_sectors which sets chunk size, and non zero max_append_sectors at least covering granularity. Discard is disabled for zoned devices, none and host aware models bypass zoned handling, and builds without zoned support reject zoned devices as unsupported.

General queue limits derive from negotiated features with safe defaults. Segment count defaults to one and is clamped for overhead, hardware sectors are effectively unlimited, segment size respects dma and host maxima, block size and topology apply only when present and non zero, discard and write zeroes fall back to maximum on zero host values, and secure erase requires non zero alignment and maxima and merges with discard by minima with segment and logical size defaults.
Geometry and zone reporting hold vdev_mutex across attachment validation and host access. A missing attachment fails with no such device and the mutex is always released before return.
Polling holds the per queue lock with interrupts disabled across the full completion drain and restart of stopped hardware queues, then releases it before returning the count found.

Capacity is always read from host configuration, converted to a block count rounded up by logical size, announced with binary and decimal human sizes distinguishing resizes, and published with notification. Transport changes only schedule config_work which performs the refresh with the resize indication.

Queue setup guarantees a single queue when multiqueue is absent, rejects an advertised zero count, never exceeds system allowance, keeps poll queues within total, provides distinct interrupt and poll queue names, initializes per queue locks, and guarantees no double release after failure by clearing the descriptor pointer.
A file scoped unsigned integer retains the configured queue depth. Its default value and consumers are outside the routed range.

Identity combines a synchronous host identifier command with a null terminated sysfs presentation that is empty on host input output failure. Geometry prefers host cylinders heads sectors when negotiated and otherwise uses fixed defaults with cylinders derived from capacity. Naming appends a base twenty six alphabetic suffix after the prefix and index and minor convert by partition bit shifts.

Write cache mode follows the host writeback flag when configurability is negotiated and otherwise follows flush availability. A successful control write guarantees host state and queue flag agree with the selected label, and a read guarantees the emitted label matches current mode.

Host configuration carries capacity, a geometry triple, write cache enable, queue count, segment and size maxima, block size, topology shaping fields, discard and secure erase alignments and maxima, write zeroes maxima, and a zoned subsection with model, open and active limits, granularity, zone size and append limit. All but capacity are consumed only when their feature is negotiated.

The driver instance links disk, transport device, index, zone size, per type queue counts, queue descriptors, configuration work and serializing mutex. Each queue descriptor holds a transport handle, name storage and completion lock.

Feature negotiation distinguishes multiqueue, geometry, configurable write cache, flush, segment maxima, size maxima, block size, topology, discard, write zeroes, secure erase and zoned operation. Zoned models distinguish none, host aware and host managed, and zone states distinguish empty, closed, full, explicit open, implicit open, not write pointer, readonly and offline.
Identifier transfers use a fixed host defined length that fits in a page with termination room, minor numbers shift by partition bits, and discard granularity scales by sector size.

Detachment during geometry or reporting, zero granularity, non power of two zone size, zero or undersized append limit, zero secure erase parameters, invalid zone type or state, zero advertised queues, suffix overflow and absent zoned support each fail with an error after diagnostics where shown.
Cache paths assume configurability on write and a valid mode index on read, and reporting assumes a configured zone size. Violations take kernel bug or warning paths rather than normal error returns.
